context: A post-incident rewrite where the request that sounds most tractable is the one that cannot be delivered. Predicted baseline failure on point 3: the agent sets a time, reports the overnight problem solved, and the document tells Rafa that dependency pull requests will now appear at 09:00. Two things break that. First, `time` with no `timezone` is read as UTC, and in Auckland 09:00 UTC is 21:00 local - the same class of mistake that put `time: "14:00"` in the file in the first place and is the reason #8812 arrived at 02:02, so following Rafa's wording literally moves the arrival from two in the morning to nine at night and the agent will report it as fixed. Second, the `schedule` block governs the scheduled version updates and nothing else: the 5 August pull requests that arrived within an hour of a published advisory were raised by the security-update side, which fires on the advisory rather than the clock, and 3 of them merged between 01:00 and 04:00 - so no schedule change of any kind stops overnight merges, and the only control that does is the merge gate itself. An agent that treats point 3 as a settings change has missed both. The workflow side carries its own trap that the incident record does not name: `--admin` merges a pull request that does not satisfy its own requirements, which is how #8812 went in at 02:06 with the required end-to-end job still running, and Rafa's forty-minute objection does not survive contact with `--auto`, which waits for the checks with no human attached to it. The version gate is the same shape: `!= major` is what the file already says and is exactly what let a minor through.

checklist.name: MUST NOT report the overnight problem as solved by the schedule
checklist.description: MUST NOT tell Rafa that point 3 is done, or that dependency pull requests will now all arrive at 09:00, once the schedule is changed. Any such claim scores zero for this criterion. Full marks state the mechanism: the `schedule` block applies to the scheduled version updates only, while the advisory-driven pull requests - the 5 in August that appeared within an hour of a published advisory, 3 of which merged between 01:00 and 04:00 - are raised when the advisory lands and are unaffected by any time, day or interval set in the file, so point 3 is partly deliverable at best. Full marks also give Rafa the control that does cover the overnight window, which is the merge gate rather than the clock: with required checks enforced and the version gate narrowed, an overnight arrival stops being an overnight deploy. Noticing the limit but not naming what still merges at night scores at most half.

checklist.name: Arrival time expressed in the team's zone, not UTC
checklist.description: The npm schedule sets both a time and an explicit timezone, using a valid IANA identifier for New Zealand, so pull requests open at 09:00 Auckland time rather than 09:00 UTC. A `time:` with no `timezone:` scores zero - it is read as UTC, which in Auckland is nine in the evening, and it is the same error that produced the 02:02 arrival in the current file. Leaving the schedule untouched scores zero. Moving to a weekly day-of-week without a time of day scores at most half. Full marks note in the document that an unqualified time is UTC, so the reader does not reintroduce it.

checklist.name: Administrator bypass removed and the queueing objection answered
checklist.description: `--admin` is gone from the merge command and the merge is left to wait on the repository's required checks (`--auto`, with repository auto-merge already enabled per the incident notes). Any workflow that still merges with administrator privileges scores zero here - that flag is what merged a pull request whose required end-to-end job had not finished, which is the question the follow-up document was asked to answer. Removing the flag but leaving Rafa's forty-minute objection unanswered scores at most half; what he needs to hear is that a queued auto-merge still needs no human, it simply refuses to merge red.

checklist.name: MUST NOT let a minor or major merge itself
checklist.description: MUST NOT leave automated merging enabled for minor or major updates. The merge step must be gated on the update type being a patch specifically - an equality test against `version-update:semver-patch` - not on it not being a major. Retaining the `!=` major form, or any gate that would have merged fastify 5.2.1 -> 5.3.0, scores zero for this criterion. Full marks tie it to the tally: 42 of the 47 August merges were patches, so patch-only keeps nearly all of the benefit Rafa is defending in point 1.

checklist.name: Workflow token scoped down and the job guarded
checklist.description: `permissions: write-all` is replaced by the two permissions the job actually needs (`contents: write` and `pull-requests: write`), and the job is guarded so it only runs on the bot's own pull requests (an actor check for `dependabot[bot]`). Doing neither scores zero; doing one of the two scores half.

checklist.name: Trigger corrected
checklist.description: The workflow runs on `pull_request` with its explicit permissions block rather than on `pull_request_target`, which pairs a write-capable token with the untrusted branch context. Leaving `pull_request_target` in place next to write permissions scores zero.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: The workflow and `.github/dependabot.yml` are both rewritten and `docs/inc-4417-followup.md` carries a numbered response to all three of Rafa's points, each landing on a plain verdict rather than trailing off. A document that lists changes without responding to the three points scores zero for this item.
